content: General regulatory factors (GRFs) such as Reb1, Abf1, Rap1, Mcm1, and Cbf1 play a critical role in organizing yeast chromatin by interacting with a core consensus DNA sequence. Ribosome biogenesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae involves a regulon of over 200 genes (Ribi genes) that are tightly regulated in response to nutrient availability and cellular growth rates. Two cis-acting elements, PAC and RRPE, mediate repression of Ribi genes during nutritional downshifts. Ribi gene promoters also contain binding sites for one or more GRFs, most commonly Abf1 and Reb1, which are enriched at Ribi promoters in vivo. The association of Abf1, Reb1, and Tbf1 with promoters is essential for full Ribi gene expression in nutrient-rich conditions and for modulating expression during glucose starvation, which is characterized by a rapid decrease followed by a slow recovery. This response does not involve changes in Abf1 occupancy but is accompanied by a rapid increase and subsequent slow decrease in Rpd3L histone deacetylase occupancy. Disruption of Abf1 binding sites abolishes the recruitment of the Rpd3L complex in response to starvation. Extensive mutational analysis of the DBP7 promoter revealed a complex interplay between Tbf1 sites, PAC, and RRPE in the transcriptional regulation of this Ribi gene. GRFs are multifaceted regulators of Ribi gene expression during both exponential growth and repressive conditions. Abf1 Regulatory Factors The general consensus sequence for Abf1, CGTNNNNN(A/G)(C/T)GA(C/T), is found on both sides of A1BG but only in the distal promoters. Random datasets yielded sequences in the UTR, core promoter, and distal promoter for the negative direction, and sequences in the distal promoter for the positive direction. The real consensus sequence produced only three results: one in the negative direction and two in the positive direction, all in distal promoters. Random sequences occurred in the UTR, proximal promoter, and distal promoter for the negative direction, and in the distal promoter for the positive direction. While the differences between real and random occurrences are small, they are likely significant, as the random datasets should have encompassed the real sequences but did not. Cbf1 Regulatory Factors The consensus sequence for Cbf1, TCACGTGA, did not yield any real or random results. Mcm1 Regulatory Factors Neither of the Mcm1 consensus sequences, TT(A/T)CCNN(A/T)TNGG(A/T)AA or TTNCCNNNTNNGGNAA, produced any real or random results. Rap1 Regulatory Factors When the Rap1 motif was fixed to ACCCRNRCA, no real results were observed. However, testing this motif and its inverse complement using ten random datasets yielded five consensus sequence results and four inverse complements. Two of these were in the UTR of A1BG from the negative direction, one was in the proximal promoter from the positive direction, and the remaining five were in distal promoters. A reduced consensus sequence, (A/G)(A/C)ACCC(A/G)N(A/G)C(A/C)(C/T)(A/C), produced one result in the positive direction at position 1807, less than halfway from ZNF497. Among ten random datasets, only one result was observed: GCACCCGGGCATC at position 1454. For the inverse complement, one result was found: TATGCCTGGGTTT at position 1380. Both real and random sequences were located in the distal promoter closer to the zinc finger than A1BG. The rarity of random results suggests that real occurrences are likely active regulatory responses. Reb1 Regulatory Factors Reb1 consensus sequences, TTACCC(G/T), occur three times in A1BG: once in the UTR at position 3661 and twice in distal promoters at positions 3170 and 2912 in the positive direction, all more than halfway from either zinc finger. Random datasets produced three sequences in two datasets within the UTR: TTACCCG at position 4135, CGGGTAA at position 3979, and AGGGTAA at position 3112. The core promoters contained only TTACCCG at position 4416 in the positive direction. The proximal promoters contained only TTACCCT at position 4250 in the positive direction. The distal promoters contained four to five sequences: five in the negative direction, all more than halfway to ZSCAN22, and four in the positive direction, including one TTACCCG at position 2965 more than halfway toward A1BG, with the remaining three less than halfway. The extended Reb1 consensus sequence, ATTACCCGAA, had no locations in either direction or in random datasets for either the extended consensus sequence or its inverse complement. Tbf1 Regulatory Factors The usual consensus sequence for Tbf1, ARCCCTAA, occurs three times around A1BG: once in the negative direction within the UTR (inverse complement TTAGGGTT at position 3978) and twice in the positive direction (negative strand TTAGGGCT at position 2768 and positive strand AACCCCTAA at position 2545). Both are closer to A1BG than either zinc finger. In the random datasets, only the inverse complements occur in one dataset: TTAGGGCT at position 3616 and TTAGGGTT at position 198, representing the positive direction in the distal promoter. The second is less than halfway from ZNF497.
